$schema_note: Machine-readable baseline of every version-dependent claim the cost-control bundle relies on. The cost-control-verify skill diffs the CURRENT Claude Code version's docs against this file, writes CHANGELOG entries, and patches the 'affects' targets. verdict/confidence are as-of baseline_verified_date. Edit via the skill, not by hand, so the changelog stays honest.

claims.summary: Which hook surface can block a subagent spawn.
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26 vs v2.1.233 docs — MECHANISM UNCHANGED again: the PreToolUse decision row, the SubagentStart context-only row, the exit-code-2 wording, and the TaskCreated lifecycle row all re-matched (link markup aside). In-range note (changelog v2.1.233 VERBATIM): 'Todo/task-tracking tools (TaskCreate/Get/Update/List, TodoWrite) are no longer available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and newer models; set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 to bring them back' — so on this install's models TaskCreated effectively never fires by default; still zero wiring impact (nothing registers on it). PRIOR PASS: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09 vs v2.1.226 docs — MECHANISM AND WORDING BOTH UNCHANGED since the v2.1.212 pass; every quote below re-matched verbatim in the current hooks.md/sub-agents.md. A subagent spawn IS a PreToolUse tool call on the `Agent` tool. sub-agents.md VERBATIM: 'In version 2.1.63, the Task tool was renamed to Agent. Existing `Task(...)` references in settings and agent definitions still work as aliases.' PreToolUse is the ONLY hook surface that can block a spawn — hooks.md decision-control table VERBATIM: 'PreToolUse | hookSpecificOutput | permissionDecision (allow/deny/ask/defer), permissionDecisionReason' (NOTE: 'defer' is a 4th value not present at the 2026-07-16 baseline; the guards only ever emit 'deny', so no change needed). `SubagentStart` CANNOT block — the current wording is NOT the baseline's 'Shows stderr to user only' but hooks.md decision-control table VERBATIM: 'SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart | Context only | hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext adds context for Claude. ... No blocking or decision control'; corroborated VERBATIM: 'For SessionStart, Setup, and SubagentStart, the exit code 2 stderr renders in the transcript as a <hook name> hook error notice ... Claude doesn't see it, and the session or subagent proceeds.' SubagentStart payload carries agent_id + agent_type only, no model (hooks.md 'SubagentStart input'). `TaskCreated` is the task-LIST event — hooks.md lifecycle table VERBATIM: 'TaskCreated | When a task is being created via TaskCreate' — unrelated to spawns; blocking it rolls back a todo item. (It also takes no matcher: 'TaskCreated ... don't support matchers and always fire on every occurrence'.)

claims.summary: Field layout of the Agent tool's tool_input as seen by PreToolUse hooks.
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26 vs v2.1.233 docs — the four tool_input fields are AGAIN byte-for-byte unchanged (hooks.md '##### Agent' table re-matched); probes stay correct. TWO REFINEMENTS to the PostToolUse cost-attribution note: (1) hooks.md now says outright that the completed-response usage fields are NOT a whole-run rollup — VERBATIM: 'for token and cost rollups across subagents, use the token and cost counters filtered to query_source "subagent", since totalTokens and usage cover the final request only' — so the 2026-08-09 'documented surface for per-subagent cost attribution' framing overstated it; telemetry counters are the documented rollup path. (2) resolvedModel semantics tightened — VERBATIM: 'On a completed response, resolvedModel names the model the subagent STARTED on'; 'On an async_launched response, resolvedModel names the model in use when the agent moved to the background'. Also in-range (changelog v2.1.232): 'Subagent forking is now on by default ... and non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now run in the background by default' — reinforcing that tool_response is usually async_launched with NO usage fields. PRIOR PASS: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09 vs v2.1.226 docs — the four tool_input fields are BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED, so the guards' probes remain correct. One addition to the PostToolUse side since the last pass: `modelsUsed` (array, 'Models used in order, with consecutive repeats collapsed; set only when the model was swapped mid-run. Requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later') — a way to detect a subagent that changed models mid-run, which resolvedModel alone would hide. Original v2.1.212 finding retained below. hooks.md 'Tool input schemas' section '##### Agent — Spawns a subagent' publishes the table VERBATIM: `prompt` (string), `description` (string), `subagent_type` (string, e.g. "Explore", 'Type of specialized agent to use'), `model` (string, e.g. "sonnet", 'Optional model alias to override the default'). This CONFIRMS the guards' primary probe paths .tool_input.model and .tool_input.subagent_type are correct; the .params.model/.opts.model fallbacks are now redundant but harmless. BONUS (PostToolUse): tool_response for a completed Agent call carries resolvedModel (v2.1.174+ — 'the model the subagent actually runs on, which can differ from the model value in tool_input'), totalTokens, totalDurationMs, totalToolUseCount, and a usage{} token breakdown — a documented surface for per-subagent cost attribution. NOTE: as of v2.1.198 subagents run in the BACKGROUND by default, so an omitted run_in_background yields status 'async_launched' and tool_response carries NO usage fields.

Ignored for [plugin subagents]', link markup added). Trust rule STRENGTHENED in wording, VERBATIM: 'This is a stricter rule than the one for hooks in settings files: trusting a parent folder isn't enough, and a -p session doesn't count as trusted.' Still moot for this install (~/.claude/agents/ exempt). PRIOR PASS: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09 vs v2.1.226 docs — field unchanged. sub-agents.md 'Supported frontmatter fields' VERBATIM: '`hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks scoped to this subagent. Ignored for plugin subagents'. Plugin caveat unchanged. NEW GATING PRECONDITION as of v2.1.218 — VERBATIM: 'To let a project-level subagent's frontmatter hooks run, accept the workspace trust dialog for the folder that contains the agent file. Hooks from user-level subagents in `~/.claude/agents/` and from definitions you pass with `--agents` run without this step. claims.summary: Do settings.json PreToolUse hooks fire for tool calls made BY a subagent?
claims.current_value: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26 vs v2.1.233 docs — the load-bearing sentence re-matched verbatim at hooks.md ('Hooks from settings files, managed policy settings, and plugins also run inside [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents). When a subagent calls a tool, tool events such as PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation...'), now ALSO corroborated in sub-agents.md: 'a PreToolUse hook in settings.json also runs before every tool a subagent uses.' Depth default still 3; fork-at-limit behavior refined, VERBATIM: 'A fork at the limit keeps Agent in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning.' PRIOR PASS: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 vs v2.1.226 docs — PARTIAL→CONFIRMED. hooks.md now states it outright, VERBATIM: 'Hooks from settings files, managed policy settings, and plugins also run inside subagents. When a subagent calls a tool, tool events such as PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation, and the input carries the agent_id and agent_type common input fields that identify the subagent.' The ambiguity that made this PARTIAL at the two prior baselines is gone: the settings-level gate DOES cover subagent-originated tool calls, including nested spawns. Consequence for the bundle: the frontmatter-replicated guard in agents/*.md is now REDUNDANCY, not the sole nested gate — keep it, because it is still the ONLY thing that would cover a case the settings gate misses, and because plugin subagents cut the other way: sub-agents.md VERBATIM 'plugin subagents don't support the hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode frontmatter fields', so plugin-shipped subagents are covered ONLY by the settings-level gate (now confirmed to fire). DEPTH LIMIT CHANGED — this is the material delta since v2.1.212: sub-agents.md VERBATIM 'By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation. At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the Agent tool from every subagent except a fork' and 'To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH to the number of subagent layers you want below your main conversation.' The prior baseline recorded 'depth five ... fixed and not configurable' — BOTH the number AND the configurability were superseded. Churn in range: v2.1.217 disabled nesting by default; v2.1.219 set the default to 3. NEW v2.1.218 TRUST CAVEAT (sub-agents.md VERBATIM): 'To let a project-level subagent's frontmatter hooks run, accept the workspace trust dialog for the folder that contains the agent file. Hooks from user-level subagents in ~/.claude/agents/ and from definitions you pass with --agents run without this step.' The bundle installs to ~/.claude/agents/ => EXEMPT, no action needed; a project-scoped copy of these agents would silently skip its frontmatter hooks in an untrusted folder ('the subagent still runs, but Claude Code skips its frontmatter hooks and logs an error to the debug log').
claims.since_version: 2.1.172 (nested spawns); 2.1.219 (depth default 3, configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH); 2.1.218 (project-level frontmatter-hook trust requirement); settings-hooks-fire-in-subagents documented as of the v2.1.226 docs

POST-LOCK heads-up (v2.1.234, NOT in this build): 'Removed the "Default teammate model" setting from /config; agent-team teammates now use the leader's model unless the spawn names one' — after the next update, an unspecified teammate model means LEADER-model cost; keep explicit models on teammate specs too. The only delta in range is the availableModels interaction (v2.1.222: a BLOCKED FAMILY ALIAS now substitutes to the newest permitted version of that family instead of falling back to the inherited model — see available-models-gate), which does not affect resolution when no allowlist is in place, as here. model-config.md env-var table VERBATIM: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is 'The model to use for all subagents, agent teams, and the agents a workflow runs. PRACTICAL EFFECT for a fable-blocking allowlist: blocking fable by omitting it entirely still lands a `model: fable` spawn on the inherited model (no fable version is permitted, so substitution has nothing to land on) — the intended gate still holds. But an allowlist that pins versions (e.g. ['sonnet','claude-opus-4-6']) will now SUBSTITUTE rather than fall back for family aliases, which is a behavior change worth knowing before placing one. v2.1.223 adds a warning when a restricted subagent model causes the parent model to run instead. enforceAvailableModels (v2.1.175+) extends it to the Default picker option. Managed paths (settings.md): macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\; managed-settings.d/*.json drop-ins merge alphabetically. Managed settings parse TOLERANTLY (invalid entries stripped with a warning; /doctor lists them); user/project/local files are STRICT (invalid file rejected as a whole). settings.md lists availableModels as settable in any scope, though model-config frames it as managed/policy — a user-scope allowlist is self-serve but also self-removable.

claims.summary: Platform-level ceilings on subagent fan-out: concurrency, nesting depth, lifetime count, and headless spend cap.
claims.current_value: NEW CLAIM added 2026-08-09 (v2.1.226). These four ceilings did not exist, or had different values, at the v2.1.212 baseline; they are the platform's own fan-out bounds and sit underneath this bundle's guards. (1) CONCURRENCY — sub-agents.md VERBATIM: 'By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry... To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to any positive whole number. Sessions with ultracode active are exempt: the limit isn't enforced there. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.' The ultracode exemption is the cost-relevant trap: ultracode removes BOTH this cap and the Large-workflow warning. (2) DEPTH — default 3 layers, set via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (see nested-spawn-hooks). (3) LIFETIME COUNT — REMOVED. sub-agents.md VERBATIM: 'There's no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session', and changelog v2.1.224 VERBATIM: 'Removed the 200-subagent-per-session spawn cap; long-running sessions no longer refuse new agents (concurrency and depth limits still apply).' A long-lived thin-brain session now has NO built-in lifetime ceiling — only burn-rate guards bound it. (4) HEADLESS SPEND CAP — cli-reference.md VERBATIM: '--max-budget-usd | Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls before stopping (print mode only). Spend from subagents counts toward the cap. Once spend reaches the cap, spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`, and Claude Code stops background subagents that are still running; the cap-enforcement behaviors require Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.' This is the only hard dollar cap available and it is print-mode only — it does NOT protect interactive sessions, which is precisely the gap guard-usage-budget.sh fills.

affects.what: fan-out guidance now names the real platform ceilings + ultracode exemption
